mainTopic: Someone forbidden by a vow to benefit from his fellow: may the fellow pay his half-shekel, repay his debt, or return his lost object? רב אושעיא and רבא explain how repaying a debt can be allowed.
overview: This amud continues a משנה about a person who is forbidden by a נדר to get any benefit from his fellow. The משנה says the fellow may still give the half-shekel for him, pay off his debt, and return his lost object. The גמרא accepts the half-shekel and the lost object, because each one is a מצוה and gives no real personal benefit. It then challenges the debt payment, since paying someone's debt seems to save him money. רב אושעיא answers that the משנה follows חנן, who holds that whoever pays another person's obligation has simply 'lost his money.' רבא answers differently: even the רבנן agree, because the case is a loan taken on the condition that the borrower need not repay it. The גמרא then asks why רב אושעיא did not accept רבא's answer. רב אושעיא's reply begins at the end of this amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What the fellow may still do for the one forbidden by the vow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three things the fellow may do for the person who is forbidden by a נדר to benefit from him: give his half-shekel, repay his debt, and return his lost object. Any reward for returning the object goes to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may give the half-shekel for him, pay off his debt, and return his lost item to him. Where people are normally paid for returning lost items, that payment goes to the Temple treasury.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the rest of a משנה that lists actions that are allowed even though one person is forbidden by a נדר to benefit from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person forbidden by a נדר may receive nothing of value from his fellow. Here the משנה says these three actions are still permitted. For the lost object, any fee normally earned for returning it is given to הקדש, so the owner gets no benefit from the fee.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives the yearly half-shekel to the Temple on his behalf

phrases.english: He may weigh out his shekel for him,
phrases.notes: This continues a משנה about a man whose נדר forbids him to benefit from his fellow. 'He' is the fellow; 'him' is the man under the vow.

phrases.english: and he may repay his debt,
and return to him his lost object.
And in a place where people take a fee,
the benefit should fall to the Temple treasury.
phrases.notes: He means the fee the finder would normally earn. It goes to הקדש instead of being given up as a favor to the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the משנה quoted before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fellow may pay the half-shekel, repay the debt, and return the lost object. Any fee for returning the object goes to הקדש.

steps.title: Giving the half-shekel is just a מצוה, not a benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that giving the half-shekel is allowed because it is a מצוה. It brings a source showing that the communal offerings already count for everyone, even for money not yet given.
steps.simpleTranslation: The half-shekel makes sense, because he is just doing a מצוה. We learned that the money for communal offerings is taken out on behalf of money that was lost, money already collected, and money still to be collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to examine the משנה. It first explains why the half-shekel is fine, and this sets up a question about the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Temple collection counts even for shekels that are lost or not yet given, every Jew already has a share in the communal offerings. So the person under the vow gains nothing personally when his shekel is paid. The fellow is simply doing a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense regarding…' (a phrase that sets up a contrast)
Withdrawing money from the Temple chamber to buy communal offerings

phrases.english: It makes sense that he may weigh out his shekel for him —
he is doing a מצוה.
As we learned:
They take out the collection on behalf of money that was lost,
phrases.notes: This is the money taken from the Temple chamber to buy the communal offerings.

phrases.english: and on behalf of money already collected,
and on behalf of money that will be collected in the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא שׁוֹקֵל לוֹ אֶת שִׁקְלוֹ — מִצְוָה קָעָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts examining the משנה by justifying its first item.
steps.raayaObject: That paying another person's half-shekel gives him no personal benefit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that the Temple collection is taken out for lost, collected, and future shekels alike.

steps.title: But repaying his debt clearly helps him
steps.stepSummary: Returning a lost object is also a מצוה. But paying off someone's debt saves him money, so it looks like forbidden benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning his lost object is also a מצוה. But paying off his debt — that surely helps him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the lost object as a מצוה. It then challenges the debt item of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the half-shekel and the lost object, paying a debt is not a מצוה done on the person's behalf. It directly saves him money he would otherwise have to pay. That seems to be exactly the benefit the נדר forbids.

phrases.english: And returning his lost object also —
he is doing a מצוה.
But repaying his debt for him —
he is surely gaining from it!
phrases.notes: Literally 'he is being rooted.' He ends up better off, since he no longer has to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פּוֹרֵעַ לוֹ אֶת חוֹבוֹ, הָא קָמִשְׁתָּרְשִׁי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'מצוה, so no benefit' reasoning from step 2 to show that the debt item does not fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to repay the debt of a person forbidden by a נדר to benefit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Paying a debt directly saves the debtor money, so it should count as forbidden benefit.

steps.title: The משנה follows חנן: the payer just lost his money
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא says the משנה follows חנן. חנן holds that someone who pays another person's obligation without being asked has 'lost his money.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: Whose view is this? It is חנן's, who said: he has lost his money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא answers the challenge by showing which תנא's view the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנן ruled that one who pays for another person's obligation has simply lost his money, and the other person does not have to pay him back. This משנה applies the same reasoning to the debt. The payer is really giving up his own money, and in a legal sense the debtor is not handed anything. Because of that, it does not count as forbidden benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: He has lost his money (he cannot collect it back)

steps.whatToRemember: Paying the half-shekel and returning a lost object are allowed because they are מצוות. According to רב אושעיא, repaying the debt is allowed because the משנה follows חנן, who holds that the payer has simply 'lost his money.' The next step gives רבא's different answer, which works even for the רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: חנן does not say the debtor gains nothing in real life. His point is that, legally, the payer has no claim and is not considered to be handing the debtor anything.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
Whose view is this? It is חנן's,
who said: he has lost his money.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier משנה in this chapter about someone who supported another man's wife while he was away.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing which תנא's view the משנה follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying someone's debt gives him a direct benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to חנן, the payer has simply lost his money and legally gives the debtor nothing, so it is not forbidden benefit.

steps.title: רבא: The loan never had to be repaid
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question differently. The משנה can follow even the רבנן, because it is talking about a loan taken on the condition that the borrower need not repay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן. Here we are dealing with someone who borrowed on the condition that he does not have to pay it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the question from Step 3. Unlike רב אושעיא, he does not need to say the משנה follows only חנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that paying someone's debt saves him money, so it looks like forbidden benefit. רבא says the משנה is about a loan the borrower never has to repay unless he chooses to. Paying it off does not really help the borrower. It mostly helps the lender, so even the רבנן would allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן (the Sages), not only חנן
Here, what case are we dealing with? (a phrase that narrows the case)
On the condition of not repaying

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not mean the borrower was given a gift. It is still a loan, but there is no pressure on the borrower to repay it. That is why paying it off is not a real favor to him.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The רבנן are the Sages who disagree with חנן, whom רב אושעיא needed in Step 4.

phrases.english: here, what are we dealing with?
where he borrowed on the condition that he need not repay.
phrases.notes: He means the borrower does not have to pay until he decides to. So paying it off really helps the lender, not him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of Step 3, in place of רב אושעיא's answer in Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the loan has no repayment obligation pressing on the borrower.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying a person's debt saves him money, so it should count as forbidden benefit, unless the משנה follows only חנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even according to the רבנן it is allowed, because the borrower of a loan with no duty to repay gains nothing real when it is paid off.

steps.title: Why didn't רב אושעיא give רבא's answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why רבא did not use רב אושעיא's answer, since רבא's answer works even for the רבנן. It then asks why רב אושעיא did not use רבא's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבא did not say like רב אושעיא, because רבא wants to explain the משנה even according to the רבנן. But רב אושעיא, why did he not say like רבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two answers and asks what made רב אושעיא avoid רבא's approach. It is setting up the next step, where רב אושעיא's reason is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer has an advantage: it fits the majority view of the רבנן. So the גמרא wonders why רב אושעיא would settle for explaining the משנה only according to חנן. There must be a problem he saw in רבא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense that (introduces the side that is understood)
He sets it up / explains the case as
But (introduces the side that is hard to understand)

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רָבָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Granted, Rava did not say like Rav Oshaya:
because he sets it up according to the Rabbis.
But Rav Oshaya,
what is the reason he did not say like Rava?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רָבָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבא's answer (Step 5) with רב אושעיא's (Step 4) and asks why רב אושעיא rejected רבא's approach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What problem did רב אושעיא see in explaining the משנה as a loan with no duty to repay?

steps.title: רב אושעיא begins his reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא starts to explain: even if the borrower gets no benefit from such a loan being paid, there is still a problem. His full reason continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא could say to you: Granted that he has no benefit,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to give רב אושעיא's answer. He admits part of רבא's point, and the rest of his answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אושעיא agrees that with this kind of loan, paying it off brings the borrower no direct money benefit. The word נהי (granted) tells us a 'but' is coming. He will point to a different problem that remains even so.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (gives a person's possible reply)
Granted that / even if (admits a point before saying 'but')

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya could say to you:
Granted that he has no benefit,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here. רב אושעיא's 'but' comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: נְהִי דַּהֲנָאָה לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the question in Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial: רב אושעיא grants that the borrower of such a loan gets no benefit when it is paid. His remaining objection continues on the next amud.
